references.text: The parents confirm here that the man is their son and that he was blind from birth, just as they do in verse 20, to avoid being expelled from the synagogue.
The father confirms that the son was blind before the healing, which is the central fact the parents uphold in verse 20 to reject the accusation that he was not blind from birth.

The parents point out that their son is an adult and can answer for himself, explaining why they confirm the facts about his condition at birth in verse 20 but leave the interpretation of the healing to him.

The motive of fear of being expelled from the synagogue is the direct reason why the parents in this chapter only confirm what is indisputable (that he is their son and was blind) and avoid confirming that Jesus is the Messiah.
